- When sentiment is consistently neutral (0.00), model tends to overestimate prices in early periods and underestimates in late periods — apply downward bias correction for later days.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast by 5–10% in the 2–3 days following a spike.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–5% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows positive sentiment (e.g., >0.20), model tends to overreact — cap forecast at 10% below the 14-day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates the first 5–7 days — add 2–3% to early-day forecasts if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment is negative (e.g., <0.00), model tends to underestimate — add 3–5% to forecast if sentiment is negative or trending down.
